text:
maya: FYI - since we rolled the new kernel-selector patch last night I'm seeing long-tail latency on the live steady-state bench. 95th and 99th jumped ~2x for a couple tenants.
liam: Noticed that too. KV hit rate for those tenants dropped ~12% in the same window. looks like different kernel choices are changing KV warmup behavior.
aj: Can you paste the profiler snippet? wondering if batching is coalescing short seqs into mini-batches and starving long seqs.
maya: Paste from perf agg: ```
kernel_choice: fast_attention_v2 -> chosen for small seqs
avg_batch_size_short: 18
avg_batch_size_long: 3
kv_hit_short: 0.82
kv_hit_long: 0.59
queue_wait_long_ms_p95: 210
queue_wait_short_ms_p95: 28
```
nora: Oof. That avg_batch_size split explains it - the short requests form dense microbatches and the allocator keeps feeding the fast kernel, leaving long seqs queued waiting for KV priming. Also seeing tenant-level token budget depletion oscillation.
liam: Reproduced locally with loadgen. Hypothesis: kernel selector's latency objective + aggressive batching threshold biases lane assignment to short-path fast kernels. Two effects: (1) long requests miss KV cache warmth due to interleaving, (2) token-credit refill penalizes long sequences because they consume credits slower but need bigger contiguous runs.
maya: Immediate mitigation: revert selector to prefer stability for >512 seqs, lower continuous-batcher max_coalesce_ms from 8 -> 4 for 30m. Rolling patch queued.
alloc-bot: deploy started by maya on infra/canary -> 3165432122 : rolling back kernel-selector v1.9 -> pinned v1.8.
aj: For medium term we should try: dynamic token-target per tenant that factors recent KV hit slope + seq-length histogram. e.g. token_target = base_target * (1 + alpha * kv_hit_delta) clipped.
liam: Also want a queue policy change: allow long-seq fast-track slot every N batches (configurable), basically preemptive slot to avoid indefinite deferral. simple param: long_preempt_every = 7.
nora: I ran a quick sim with long_preempt_every=7 + token_target alpha=0.4 and saw p95 for long tenants drop 40% while short medians unaffected. attaching numbers: p95_long before: 210ms -> after: 125ms. kv_hit_long: 0.59 -> 0.73.
maya: Nice. Can we implement a lightweight telemetry flag to emit "kv_hit_slope" and "batch_affinity" per tenant for 48h so we can A/B? want to avoid over-instrumentation but need these signals to tune alpha and preempt frequency.
liam: I'll add a temporary trace in the packet microbatcher and a metric in the per-tenant summary. aj can wire the allocator to consume token_target override.
aj: Will submit PR for the allocator hooks and config knobs. plan: short rollout to canary, collect 24h, then gradual to tiered pools.
maya: For the perf regression root-cause: file an RCA note linking kernel-selector telemetry to batching stats + KV hit deltas. Mark P0 for next sprint to avoid recurrence.
nora: One more thought: kernel selection should use a faint inertia term to avoid flip-flopping within short windows. e.g. prefer last_chosen_kernel with small penalty instead of stateless argmax. avoids churn.
liam: Agree. Put that on the kernel-selector refactor list.
maya: Thanks all — tracking in the board. will post results after 24h canary. :thumbsup:
